mainTopic: Whether a second קידושין can take effect after a divorce, compared to בר פדא's case of redeemed הקדש saplings; then the start of a new משנה about vows against 'seafarers' and 'land-dwellers'.
overview: The גמרא tries to use בר פדא's rule about redeemed saplings to answer רב הושעיא's question. בר פדא holds that consecrated saplings become הקדש again after they are redeemed. רב הושעיא asked about a man who gives a woman two פרוטות: 'with one be betrothed to me today, and with the other after I divorce you.' The idea is that the second betrothal would take hold after the divorce, just as the saplings become holy again. רבי ירמיה wakes up and rejects the comparison. Quoting רבי יוחנן, he explains that saplings become holy again only if the owner himself redeemed them, not if others did. A divorced woman is like the case where others redeemed them. A separate report from רבי אמי in the name of רבי יוחנן confirms this distinction. Then a new משנה teaches that a vow against seafarers does not forbid land-dwellers, but a vow against land-dwellers does forbid seafarers. It also defines a seafarer as someone who sails far, not someone going from עכו to יפו. The גמרא reports that רב פפא and רב אחא בריה דרב איקא disagree about which clause that definition belongs to. It begins spelling out the first opinion, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Using בר פדא to answer רב הושעיא's question about a second betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The scholars suggest that בר פדא's rule proves the second קידושין in רב הושעיא's case would work.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can now answer רב הושעיא's question. He asked about a man who gives a woman two פרוטות and says: 'With one, be betrothed to me today; with the other, be betrothed to me after I divorce you.' Based on בר פדא, the second betrothal should also be valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars try to settle an open question of רב הושעיא using בר פדא's view about saplings that become הקדש again after being redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר פדא holds that saplings that were consecrated and then redeemed automatically become הקדש again, because the original declaration still applies. Likewise, once the first marriage ends with a גט, the earlier second betrothal could kick in automatically. So רב הושעיא's question would be answered: yes, it is valid קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Resolve it, meaning 'answer the open question from here'
The smallest coin; enough to make a betrothal
Be betrothed to me (the formula of קידושין)
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: Resolve from here what Rav Hoshaya asked:
phrases.notes: The proof is בר פדא's saplings, discussed just before this, which become holy again after being redeemed.

phrases.english: One who gives two perutot to a woman
and says to her: 'With one, be betrothed to me today,
and with the other, be betrothed to me after I divorce you.'
So too, it should be a valid betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of בר פדא's view by applying it to רב הושעיא's question.
steps.raayaObject: That the second betrothal in רב הושעיא's case takes effect after the divorce.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בר פדא's ruling that redeemed saplings automatically become הקדש again.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה shows the two cases are different
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה rejects the comparison. Saplings go back to הקדש only when the owner himself redeemed them, and a divorced woman is like the case where others redeemed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה woke up and said to them: Why are you comparing a case where he redeemed them to a case where others redeemed them? This is what רבי יוחנן said: if he redeemed them, they become holy again. If others redeemed them, they do not become holy again. And a woman is like a case where others redeemed her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה, who had been dozing, overhears and knocks down the proof from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר פדא's rule only works when the owner redeems the saplings himself, because they are still in his hands. Once others redeem them, they are out of his control, so his old declaration cannot take hold again. After a גט the woman is fully independent of her husband, like saplings redeemed by others. So the second betrothal does not automatically take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Woke up
You are comparing
He redeemed them (from הקדש)
They become holy (הקדש) again

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה is not saying the woman stays married. 'Others redeemed' is a picture: after the divorce she is no longer under the husband's control, just as saplings redeemed by someone else are out of the owner's control.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya woke up and heard them,
he said to them: Why are you comparing
where he redeemed them to where others redeemed them?
This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
If he redeemed them, they become holy again;
if others redeemed them, they do not become holy again.
And a woman is like a case where others redeemed her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מְדַּמֵּיתוּן פְּדָאָן הוּא לִפְדָאוּם אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using בר פדא to resolve רב הושעיא's question; it does not reject בר פדא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof ignores the difference between the owner redeeming and others redeeming. A divorced woman matches the 'others redeemed' case, where the old declaration does not take hold again.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the limit of בר פדא's rule: an earlier declaration can take hold again only while the item is still in the declarer's control.

steps.title: רבי אמי's report confirms רבי יוחנן's distinction
steps.stepSummary: A separate report from רבי אמי in the name of רבי יוחנן confirms that בר פדא's rule applies only when the owner himself redeemed the saplings.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי אמי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: they only taught this when he himself redeemed them. But if others redeemed them, they do not become holy again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another report that supports רבי ירמיה's version of רבי יוחנן's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה quoted רבי יוחנן on his own. Now an independent chain, רבי אמי quoting רבי יוחנן, says the same thing. This confirms that בר פדא's 'becomes holy again' is limited to the owner's own redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (a supporting report)
They only taught this in the case of

steps.whatToRemember: בר פדא's 'they become holy again' applies only if the owner himself redeemed the saplings. A divorced woman is like 'others redeemed', so רב הושעיא's question cannot be settled from בר פדא.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
They only taught this where he himself redeemed them,
phrases.notes: 'This' means בר פדא's rule that the saplings become holy again.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל פְּדָאוּם אֲחֵרִים — אֵין חוֹזְרוֹת וּקְדוֹשׁוֹת.
phrases.english: but if others redeemed them, they do not become holy again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the distinction רבי ירמיה made in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's distinction between the owner redeeming and others redeeming.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An independent report: רבי אמי in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Redeemed saplings become הקדש again only if the owner redeemed them himself.

steps.title: New משנה: vowing against seafarers versus land-dwellers
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on a נדר against seafarers and against land-dwellers. A vow against land-dwellers also includes seafarers.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who vows not to benefit from those who go down to the sea is allowed to benefit from those who live on dry land. Someone who vows against those who live on dry land is forbidden to benefit from seafarers too, because seafarers are included among those who live on dry land.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with how we understand the group names a person uses in a נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'seafarers' is narrow, so a vow against them does not include ordinary land-dwellers. 'Land-dwellers' is broad: seafarers also live on land between voyages. So they are included in that vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
One who makes a vow (נדר)
Seafarers, literally 'those who go down to the sea'
Those who live on dry land
Included within

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who vows not to benefit from seafarers
is permitted to benefit from those who live on dry land.
If he vowed against those who live on dry land, he is forbidden from seafarers too,
because seafarers are included among those who live on dry land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic; the previous discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow against seafarers does not forbid land-dwellers. A vow against land-dwellers forbids seafarers too, since they are included.

steps.title: Who counts as a seafarer
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines 'seafarers' as people who regularly sail far away, not people taking short coastal trips.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not like those who travel from עכו to יפו, but someone whose way is to set out on long voyages.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains exactly what 'seafarers' means for these vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A short boat trip along the coast, like from עכו to יפו, does not make someone a 'seafarer'. The term means people who regularly sail out on long journeys, so only they fall under a vow against seafarers.

keyTerms.meaning: Akko, a port city in northern ארץ ישראל
Jaffa, a port city further south along the coast
To set out (on long sea voyages)

steps.whatToRemember: In vows, people's words follow their normal meaning. 'Land-dwellers' is broad and includes seafarers. 'Seafarers' means only real long-distance sailors.

phrases.english: Not like those who travel from Akko to Jaffa,
phrases.notes: This is a short trip along the same coast, so it doesn't count.

phrases.english: but rather someone whose way is to set out on voyages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term 'seafarers' used in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Seafarers' means people who regularly sail long distances, not those who take short coastal trips.

steps.title: Two אמוראים disagree about where the seafarer definition belongs
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב אחא בריה דרב איקא disagree. One attaches the משנה's definition of seafarers to the first clause, and the other attaches it to the last clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב פפא and רב אחא, son of רב איקא, disagree. One teaches the definition on the first clause, and the other teaches it on the last clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by reporting a disagreement about which part of the משנה the definition of 'seafarers' explains. This line sets up the next move: step 7 starts explaining the first opinion, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has two clauses: a vow against seafarers (the רישא) and a vow against land-dwellers (the סיפא). It also defines seafarers as people who sail far away, not people on short coastal trips. The question is which clause that definition explains, and the answer can change who is permitted and who is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה
The last clause of a משנה
Teaches or attaches (a statement to a certain place)
One (of them)

steps.confusionAlert: Neither opinion changes the משנה's two basic rulings. They disagree about which clause the line about עכו and יפו belongs to, and attaching it to a different clause can change what that line means.

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika:
one teaches it on the first clause
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה's definition of seafarers from the last step: people who sail far away, not short coastal trips.

phrases.english: and one teaches it on the last clause

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד מַתְנֵי אַרֵישָׁא וְחַד מַתְנֵי אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in steps 4-5, asking which clause the seafarer definition explains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a disagreement about whether the seafarer definition belongs to the vow against seafarers (רישא) or to the vow against land-dwellers (סיפא).

steps.title: The first opinion: the definition explains the vow against seafarers
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that attaches the definition to the first clause reads the משנה like this: someone who vows against seafarers may still benefit from land-dwellers but not from seafarers. The definition then tells us who counts as a seafarer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches it on the first clause reads it like this: Someone who vows against seafarers is permitted to benefit from land-dwellers, but is forbidden to benefit from seafarers, and 'seafarers' does not mean those...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the first opinion by reading the definition into the first clause. The sentence continues in the next section of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the line about עכו and יפו is attached to the vow against seafarers. It tells us which travelers this vow covers, not which land-dwellers it covers. The sentence breaks off at 'and not like those', and the next amud spells out exactly how this opinion reads the definition.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a vow (here, a vow not to benefit from someone)
Seafarers, people who go down to the sea
Land-dwellers, people who live on dry land
But (in contrast)

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the first clause
teaches it like this:
One who vows not to benefit from seafarers
is permitted to benefit from land-dwellers,
but from seafarers he is forbidden,
and not like those...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the disagreement introduced in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first opinion, a vow against seafarers allows land-dwellers but forbids seafarers, and the line about עכו and יפו is read as part of this first clause.
